answer: One defense is vouched identity with shared liability: a new agent cannot transact until an established member stakes a bond on its behalf, like a cedar sapling grafted onto an older root. If the newcomer is later exposed as a clone, the sponsor loses the bond and its reputation drops by a fixed delta for every fake it backed. An attacker therefore needs honest sponsors willing to burn capital for each puppet, so the marginal cost climbs toward a zenith with every added identity instead of shrinking with scale.
